days.title: Day 1
days.note: Lower Goodell Creek TH to a col near the Chopping Block (~6+ mi, ~6,000 ft gain).

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Traverse Crescent Creek Basin, cross to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, rappel onto the Mustard Glacier, then climb the North Buttress (9 pitches, 5.9, ~2,000 ft).

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-4 day trip out of Goodell Creek Trailhead: a long, brutal cross-country approach over the Barrier to a high camp in/above Crescent Creek Basin, a big summit day tagging East (and usually West) Twin Needle via Eye Col, an optional spare/bonus day, and a long descent back out — roughly 16-19 miles round trip and 7,000+ ft of cumulative gain.

days.title: Approach over the Barrier to high camp
days.objective: Reach camp in/above Crescent Creek Basin
days.note: A grueling cross-country day: old roadbed and steep, brushy boot path from Goodell Creek Trailhead past Terror Creek, then a loose, exposed scramble across the Barrier into the Crescent Creek Basin drainage. Most parties camp on a flat bench or col around 6,000-6,400 ft, close under the Chopping Block/Twin Needles grou…

days.title: East (and West) Twin Needle via Eye Col
days.objective: Summit East Twin Needle, tag West Twin Needle if conditions allow
days.note: An alpine-start day from camp: cross Crescent Creek Basin's snow and talus to Eye Col, the notch between the two Twin Needles, then scramble/climb the South Route to East Twin Needle's summit. Most parties use the same col to tack on West Twin Needle's easier class 2-3 west slope before returning to camp.

days.title: Spare day / bonus objective
days.objective: Weather buffer or add a second Southern Pickets peak
days.note: Built-in slack for weather or recovery. Strong parties instead use it to climb another objective from the same camp, commonly Himmelhorn or Mount Terror's West Ridge, at similar cost in time and effort to Day 2.

days.title: Descend back to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek Trailhead
days.note: A long reversal of Day 1: break camp, re-cross the Barrier, and descend the steep boot path and roadbed back to the car. Most parties treat this as a full day given the terrain and fatigue.

campsite_pins.name: Chopping Block saddle camp (above Crescent Creek Basin)

trip_plan.totalNote: Three days: bushwhack up the Barrier to a Chopping Block ridge camp, a very long day over the Otto-Himmel col to climb the couloir and return, then descend to Goodell Creek.

days.title: Goodell Creek to Chopping Block ridge camp
days.objective: Climb the Barrier to camp on Chopping Block ridge
days.note: Walk the old Goodell Creek road and trail, cross Terror Creek on a high log, then grind up roughly 1,700 ft of steep, cliff-broken bushwhacking on a faint boot path to the ridge crest. Continue up snow below the Chopping Block to a flattened camp spot on the ridge.

days.title: Climb Thread of Ice and return to camp
days.objective: Climb the couloir to Eye Col and the East Twin Needle
days.note: Cross Crescent Creek Basin to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then drop about 1,000 ft down its north side and the glacier to the foot of the Thread. The couloir is about 1,200 ft of hard snow and near-ice to Eye Col; the East Needle is a short Class 3-4 scramble from there, and the south-side gullies take downclimbing an…

days.title: Descend the Barrier to Goodell Creek
days.objective: Return to the car
days.note: Reverse the ridge, the Barrier bushwhack and the Terror Creek log; the boot path is easy to lose on the ridge. The first-ascent party called it a five-hour descent.

trip_plan.totalNote: A remote, non-technical-camp-to-technical-summit trip: roughly 4 days and ~18 miles round trip with ~7,600 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on Day 1 and the Day 4 exit, bracketing a short but serious Barrier crossing and a roped scramble/ridge day to tag the summit.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin
days.objective: Establish first high camp at ~5,800 ft in Terror Basin
days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead, follow an old roadbed and climbers' path up Terror Creek through timber to treeline, then boulder-hop/scramble to a camp near 5,800 ft in Terror Basin, just below the saddle leading toward the Barrier. This mirrors the standard Southern Pickets approach day used for Inspiration, Terror…

days.title: Cross the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Cross 'The Barrier' and set up camp near Crescent Creek Basin (~6,200 ft)
days.note: A short but serious day: sustained Class 3 scrambling up loose, grassy ledges to the Barrier crest (~6,400-6,600 ft), exposed but well-traveled, then down the far side into Crescent Creek Basin to camp near 6,200 ft below the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn massif. Parties often arrive early enough to scout the col or bag an easy …

days.title: Summit push: over the col to Frenzel Spitz
days.objective: Cross the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, descend its north side and climb Frenzel Spitz
days.note: An alpine-start day climbing roughly an hour up scrambling terrain from camp to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then rappelling and downclimbing roughly 500 ft of broken couloir and glacier/moat terrain off the col's north side to the foot of Frenzel Spitz's south face, and climbing its 5.6 rock to the summit. days.title: Exit: back over the Barrier to the trailhead
days.objective: Break camp, re-cross the Barrier, and hike out to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Pack up Crescent Creek Basin camp, re-cross the Barrier back into Terror Basin, and continue the long descent down Terror Creek to the trailhead. Fit parties do this in one long push, similar in reverse to Days 1-2 combined; some choose to split it into two shorter days if the group is tired or weather is closing in.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip out of Goodell Creek: a long, brushy, steep approach day to Crescent Creek Basin (~5,300 ft gain), a technical scramble day up the Otto-Himmel col gully to the 7,880 ft summit and back to camp, and a full day hiking out — roughly 16-17 miles and 7,700 ft of gain/loss round trip.

days.title: Approach to Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Reach high camp below Himmelhorn
days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead, follow an old roadbed about 4-4.5 miles, then leave the maintained trail to climb the brushy forested ridge crest, cross Terror Creek on a log jam, and continue through Stump Hollow into Crescent Creek Basin. It's a steep, brushy, unmaintained climbers' path with route-finding required…

days.title: Climb Himmelhorn (Standard Route) and return to camp
days.objective: Summit Himmelhorn via the Otto-Himmel col gully
days.note: An alpine-start day climb from Crescent Creek Basin: ascend the narrow snow/scree gully to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then work up the northwest side to the summit, downclimbing or bypassing an overhanging block near the top on class 3/4 rock in late season. Descend by reversing the route, downclimbing and rappelling…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach: back across Crescent Creek Basin and Stump Hollow, over the ridge crest, down through the brush to the old roadbed and out to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: Three days minimum: a long approach over the Barrier to a camp below the Chopping Block, a 4 am start for the 8-pitch south face, and a 7-hour walk out.

days.title: Goodell Creek to Chopping Block camp
days.objective: Reach a camp below the Chopping Block
days.note: Follow the old Goodell Creek roadbed about 4 miles to the Terror Creek turnoff near 1,700 ft, then take the steep climbers' path up the Barrier to timberline around 5,000-5,600 ft. Continue through Stump Hollow to the crest near 6,400 ft and camp below the Chopping Block above Crescent Creek. Many parties split this in…

days.title: Climb Stonehenge on the Himmelhorn
days.objective: Climb the south face to the summit and return to camp
days.note: Cross to the snow below the wall, then scramble about 600 ft of easy ramps and ledges to a grassy col and rope up. Eight pitches include two 5.10- leads: a dihedral-to-hand-crack on pitch 2 and a run-out face on the summit tower. An unprotected traverse to a notch ends the difficulties before an easy, loose pitch to th…

days.title: Barrier and Goodell Creek to the car
days.objective: Walk out to the trailhead
days.note: Retrace through Stump Hollow and down the Barrier, crossing Terror Creek on a log near 2,000 ft before rejoining the roadbed. Abegg's party took about 7 hours from the Chopping Block camp to the car.

trip_plan.totalNote: Three days: approach over the Barrier into the Crescent Creek side, climb the gully to the Himmel-Otto col and four pitches to the summit, then walk out in about 7 hours.

days.title: Goodell Creek over the Barrier
days.objective: Reach a camp above Crescent Creek Basin
days.note: Take the Goodell Creek roadbed about 4 miles to the Terror Creek turnoff, climb the steep Barrier path to timberline, and traverse Stump Hollow to the saddle near 6,400 ft. Good bivies sit below Terror in Crescent Creek Basin, with a decent one just below the Himmel-Otto col. Many parties take two days for this approac…

days.title: Gully to the col and Wild Hair Crack
days.objective: Climb to the Himmelhorn summit and return to camp
days.note: Climb the narrow gully to the Himmel-Otto col. Early in the season it is all snow with a little scrambling near the top; late in the season expect icy snow, chossy moats, and a loose class 3-4 bypass of an overhanging boulder. Four pitches of 5.7 PG13 lead to the summit. Descend by scrambling early season, or rappel th…

days.title: Walk out to Goodell Creek
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: Reverse Stump Hollow and the Barrier, cross Terror Creek near 2,000 ft, and follow the roadbed back. Abegg's party took about 7 hours from the Chopping Block camp.

trip_plan.totalNote: A demanding 3-day trip (~21 mi, ~7,800 ft total gain): same Terror Basin approach as the other routes, but the summit day is an 18-hour epic combining 10 pitches up and 14 rappels down two different ridges/faces.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin
days.objective: Establish camp in Terror Basin
days.note: Same brutal approach shared by all Inspiration Peak routes: brushy Goodell Creek trail, then a steep ~3,600+ ft forested slog with no switchbacks up to a saddle and down into Terror Basin camp.

days.title: Climb the East Ridge
days.objective: Summit Inspiration Peak (7,891') via the East Ridge and get back to camp
days.note: An all-day alpine outing: scramble and glacier-travel to the route start, then climb 4 pitches of 5.7 to gain the ridge crest, a 5.8 pitch and the 5.9 crack crux, then 4 more moderate pitches to the summit (~8 hrs of climbing). There is no walk-off — the descent is 5 rappels down the upper West Ridge, a scramble to a n…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: After the previous day's marathon push, most parties take a slower exit hike back down to the trailhead; road closures on Highway 20 can add hours to the drive home, so budget extra time.

camps_on_file.name: Terror Basin camp
camps_on_file.notes: The base camp for the whole Southern Pickets and the one this route is built around: parties sleep here, climb, and come back to it, so plan two nights rather than moving camp. It sits about 400 ft below the 6,200 ft saddle the approach crosses, with flowers, running water and a full view of the range. The approach to …

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip out of Goodell Creek: ~21 mi round trip and ~7,500 ft total gain, with one very long summit day (~14-15 hrs) sandwiched between a brutal bushwhack approach and exit.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin
days.objective: Establish camp in Terror Basin
days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead, hike ~4 mi of brushy trail along the creek, then grind up an unrelenting, viewless ~3,600 ft of steep forested slope with no switchbacks, finishing with a rising traverse to a ~6,200 ft saddle and a short descent into Terror Basin. Real trip reports clock this leg at roughly 6.5 hours.

days.title: Climb the West Ridge
days.objective: Summit Inspiration Peak (7,891') via the West Ridge and return to camp
days.note: A long alpine day: cross the Terror Glacier (crampons on, watch for the mid-glacier icefall), gain the base of the ridge, then climb ~14 pitches of sustained 5.6-5.7 rock to the summit. Descend the same ridge crest by rappel/downclimb combo back to the glacier and camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach: scree/scramble up out of the basin, over the saddle, and down the steep forested slope back to the creek trail. Most parties take it easier than the way in but still budget most of a day given the terrain.

camps_on_file.name: Terror Basin camp
camps_on_file.notes: This is the standard base camp for the whole Southern Pickets and a genuinely comfortable one — a small flat gravelly basin with flowers, running water and a full view of the range, sitting about 400 ft below the notch in the ridge above it. It is a planned camp, not a bivy: parties sleep here, climb the peak, and come…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip (~21 mi, ~7,800 ft total gain) built around the same Terror Basin approach; the South Face itself is the shortest of Inspiration's technical routes (just 4 pitches), making for a noticeably shorter summit day than the East or West Ridges.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin
days.objective: Establish camp in Terror Basin
days.note: Same approach as the other Inspiration Peak routes: brushy creek trail followed by a steep, unrelenting forested climb to a saddle and down into Terror Basin. One party clocked this at about 6.5 hours to the 5,800 ft lower basin camp.

days.title: Climb the South Face

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach back down to the trailhead — steep, slow, and tiring on tired legs, but typically the easiest of the three days.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin high camp
days.objective: Reach Terror Basin camp (~5,800 ft)
days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead (600 ft), follow the old forestry-road bed roughly 4 miles through mossy, brushy, deadfall-choked forest, then turn uphill at the cairned junction for a steep 2-mile, ~4,000 ft climb through heather benches and blueberry fields to the notch overlooking Terror Basin. days.title: Summit day: West Ridge of West McMillan Spire
days.objective: Climb the Terror Glacier snow finger and West Ridge to the 8,004 ft summit and back to camp
days.note: An early start puts the party on the Terror Glacier's snow finger while it's still firm; the glacier crossing is typically done unroped with axe/crampons to the col, where terrain transitions to class 3 rock for the West Ridge scramble to the summit. Most parties are back in camp by late morning after a round trip of a…

days.title: Hike out to the trailhead
days.objective: Break camp and descend to Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Pack up camp, climb back up out of the basin to the notch, then descend the heather benches and forested old road bed back to the car — mostly downhill and noticeably faster than the way in, though the deadfall-choked lower trail still slows the pace.

camps_on_file.name: Terror Basin camp
camps_on_file.notes: The planned camp for this route and effectively the only one — a flat gravelly basin roughly 400 ft below and north of the 6,200 to 6,350 ft notch that the approach crosses. Comfortable ground, water at hand, and a direct view of the Pickets. From here it is a long traverse over benches and slabs to the Terror Glacier …

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip (commonly climbed as part of a longer Southern Pickets outing): ~18.7 miles round trip with roughly 7,500 ft of gain/loss, one long approach day, one big summit day with a rappel, and one exit day.

days.title: Approach to high camp
days.objective: Reach Terror Basin / Stump Hollow high camp (~5,800–6,200 ft)
days.note: A long, brutal bushwhack: Goodell Creek Trail to a fading climbers' path, a tricky ford of Terror Creek, then a steep, sustained climbers' trail straight up the hillside to treeline and on to a bench near The Barrier. This leg typically takes 6.5–9.5 hours depending on creek levels and route-finding.

days.title: Climb Degenhardt via the Southwest/Corkscrew Route
days.objective: Summit Mount Degenhardt (8,107 ft) and return to high camp
days.note: An alpine-start round trip from camp: cross The Barrier via the upper crossing just below Degenhardt into Crescent Basin, then climb a Class 4 slot to the north ridge, a Class 4-5 face to the west ridge, and an exposed Class 3 ledge to the south ridge and summit. One rappel off the summit block on the way down; loose, …

days.title: Exit to trailhead
days.objective: Hike out to the Goodell Creek Cross-Country Access Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the Day 1 approach: down the steep hillside, re-ford Terror Creek, and follow the climbers' path and Goodell Creek Trail back to the car. Descending is a bit faster than the grind up but still a full day with the creek crossing.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 4-day trip: two hard bushwhack approach days to Crescent Creek Basin, one very long (14-15 hr) technical day on the 2,500 ft North Face / North Buttress line, and a day to hike out.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin / Stump Hollow
days.objective: Reach camp in Terror Basin below the Southern Pickets
days.note: From the Goodell Creek Trailhead (600 ft), follow the old road bed to the cairn near 1,700 ft, then turn hard right up the steep Terror Basin climbers' path to camp in Terror Basin (about 5,800 ft). This is widely considered one of the harder approaches in the Cascades; expect route-finding and heavy brush even in good…

days.title: Move to Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Position camp below the peak's south/east side
days.note: Cross the Barrier and traverse into Crescent Creek Basin (~5,800 ft), staying high along the bushy ridge. Short mileage but slow, exposed sidehill travel; many parties treat this as a half-day and use the rest to scout the route or rest before the summit push.

days.title: North Face / North Buttress summit push
days.objective: Climb the 2,500 ft North Face and return to camp
days.note: A long alpine day: cross the Otto-Himmel col and traverse below the Twin Spires and the Rake to reach the base of the North Face, then climb the face and its right-hand buttress (5.7, much of it simul-climbed) to the 8,151 ft summit before descending the West Ridge gully to get back to camp.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Goodell Creek Trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach: back over the Barrier, down through Terror Basin, and down the Terror Basin climbers' path to the trailhead. Brush is easier to push through downhill but navigation errors are still common.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 4-day trip: two approach days to Crescent Creek Basin, then a shorter (~9 hr) summit day on the short, steep 4-pitch East Ridge above camp, and a day out. This is the least-popular of Terror's routes and is usually done as one leg of a larger Southern Pickets enchainment rather than a standalone objective.

days.title: Approach to Terror Basin / Stump Hollow
days.objective: Reach the 6,000 ft basin below the Southern Pickets
days.note: From the Goodell Creek Trailhead (600 ft), follow the old road bed about 4.5 miles to the cairns, then turn hard right up the steep Terror Basin climbers' path to camp in Terror Basin around 5,800 ft. Reserve a full day; this approach is a known crux of the trip in its own right.

days.title: Move to Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Position camp below the Terror-Degenhardt saddle
days.note: Cross the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin (~5,800 ft) and camp near the base of the slabs leading up to the saddle between Terror and Degenhardt. A shorter day than Day 1, used to rest and stage for the climb.

days.title: East Ridge summit push
days.objective: Climb the 4-pitch East Ridge to the summit and return
days.note: A more moderate day than the north-side routes: slabs lead directly from camp to the saddle between Terror and Degenhardt, then a short, steep 4-pitch ridge/face climbs straight to the top, then descended by the West Ridge gully, with rappels, back into Crescent Creek Basin and camp.

days.title: Hike out

days.note: Reverse the approach: back over the Barrier, down through Terror Basin, and down the Terror Basin climbers' path to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: Hike to a high camp in Crescent Creek Basin, make a very long alpine-start day over the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and Mustard Glacier to climb the buttress and descend the West Ridge notch, then hike out.

days.title: Hike to Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Reach the high camp in Crescent Creek Basin
days.note: Hike to the high camp in Crescent Creek Basin via Terror Creek, the Barrier, Stump Hollow, and the 6,400 ft saddle northeast of The Chopping Block, then downclimb about 200 ft into the basin. Expect about 6,000 ft of gain and 7-7.5 hours.

days.title: Climb the Stoddard Buttress
days.objective: Climb the buttress to the summit and return to camp
days.note: Make an alpine start, cross the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and Mustard Glacier to the route base (2-3 hours from camp), and climb the buttress crest and knife-edge finish to the summit. Descend via the West Ridge notch and gully rappels; it is a long day, about 17 hours camp to camp for one party.

days.note: Hike out.

days.title: Climb the West Ridge
days.objective: Summit via the West Ridge notch and return to camp
days.note: Climb the gully to the West Ridge notch, complete the short technical section and summit scramble, then descend the same way.
